Porter Martone, the sixth overall pick in 2025, is in his first full NHL season at 20 and already living with the noise that comes with it. Broad Street Hockey wrote about what he needs to save his Calder Trophy hopes. Then came a report that Travis Konecny was frustrated about being passed on the depth chart by him, which Flyers reporter Charlie O'Connor openly doubted, pointing out that Martone averages about 14 minutes a night.

On the ice, the problem is narrow. He hasn't scored in 11 games, but he generated 2.6 expected goals in that stretch; the pucks just aren't going in. Five of his nine points have come on the power play, he throws his weight around (39 hits), and the Flyers do better with him on the ice than without, about six and a half points in expected-goal share.

Among forwards picked fourth to eighth since 2005, the median first season was 0.44 points a game; he's at 0.38. That's close enough to call it a normal rookie year with bad luck attached. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 70% of his shots coming off the rush in a small sample, so watch him in transition.
headline: Martone's goals are late, not gone
